facts.statement: Aviatyrannis is a small coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of Portugal that is classified as either a tyrannosauroid or an ornithomimosaurian.
facts.quote: Aviatyrannis is a genus of coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur, either a tyrannosauroid or an ornithomimosaurian, from the Oxfordian-Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic found in Portugal.

facts.statement: Oliver Walter Mischa Rauhut first reported tyrannosauroid material found in the Guimarota lignite coal mine near Leiria in 2000, initially referring it to Stokesosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2000 Oliver Walter Mischa Rauhut reported the find of tyrannosauroid material in the lignite coal mine of Guimarota near Leiria, which he referred to Stokesosaurus.

facts.statement: Rauhut named and described the new genus Aviatyrannis with the type species Aviatyrannis jurassica in 2003 after concluding the material was distinct enough from Stokesosaurus.
facts.quote: Later concluding the distinctiveness of the material justified a separate genus, Rauhut in 2003 named and described it as the type species Aviatyrannis jurassica.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, IPFUB Gui Th 1, consists of a right ilium found in the early Kimmeridgian Alcobaça Formation approximately 155 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype, IPFUB Gui Th 1, was found in a layer of the Alcobaça Formation dating from the early Kimmeridgian, about 155 million years old. It consists of a right ilium.

facts.statement: In 2003, Rauhut referred two additional bones, a partial right ilium and a right ischium, to the genus Aviatyrannis.
facts.quote: Rauhut in 2003 referred two other bones to Aviatyrannis: IPFUB Gui Th 2, a partial right ilium, and IPFUB Gui Th 3, a right ischium.

facts.statement: Sixteen isolated teeth were referred to Aviatyrannis, including three from the premaxilla and thirteen from the maxilla and dentary.
facts.quote: Additionally sixteen isolated teeth were referred: IPFUB GUI D 89-91: three teeth of the premaxilla, and IPFUB GUI D 174-186: thirteen teeth of the maxilla and dentary.

facts.statement: Aviatyrannis was a small theropod, with the holotype ilium measuring only ninety millimeters in length.
facts.quote: Aviatyrannis was a rather small theropod. The holotype specimen IPFUB Gui Th 1, for example, is an ilium only ninety millimeters long.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Aviatyrannis at 1 meter and its body mass at 4 kilograms, suggesting the holotype might be a juvenile.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 1 m and its body mass at 4 kg; he also suggested that the holotype possibly belongs to a juvenile.

facts.statement: The ilium of Aviatyrannis is elongated and low, featuring a vertical ridge typical of tyrannosauroids above the hip joint.
facts.quote: The ilium is elongated and low with the typical tyrannosauroid vertical ridge on the outer blade surface above the hip joint.

facts.statement: The teeth of the praemaxilla in Aviatyrannis have a D-shaped cross-section.
facts.quote: The teeth of the praemaxilla have a D-shaped cross-section.

facts.statement: The maxillary and dentary teeth of Aviatyrannis are elongated, recurving only near the top, and possess perpendicular denticles on both edges.
facts.quote: The maxillary and dentary teeth are elongated, only recurving near the top, with perpendicular denticles on both edges.

facts.statement: Rauhut placed Aviatyrannis in the Tyrannosauroidea in a basal position in 2003.
facts.quote: Aviatyrannis was in 2003 by Rauhut placed in the Tyrannosauroidea, in a basal position.

facts.statement: If classified as a tyrannosauroid, Aviatyrannis is one of the oldest known members of that group, potentially older than Proceratosaurus.
facts.quote: If this placement is correct, Aviatyrannis is one of the oldest tyrannosauroids ever found, the oldest being Proceratosaurus (or, possibly, Iliosuchus).

facts.statement: A 2023 study noted that the Aviatyrannis ilium is strikingly similar to that of the deinocheirid Tyrannomimus.
facts.quote: However, a 2023 paper by Hattori et al. noted that the Aviatyrannis ilium is strikingly similar to that of the newly described deinocheirid Tyrannomimus.

facts.statement: Aviatyrannis was small, with the holotype ilium measuring only 90 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: El aviatiranis era pequeño, solo llegaba a los 90 centímetros de largo y 30 de alto, por ejemplo el holotipo, un ilion (IPFUB Gui Th 1), solo medía 90 milímetros.

facts.statement: Like other primitive tyrannosauroids, Aviatyrannis was a small bipedal predator.
facts.quote: Al igual que otros tiranosauroides primitivoss, Aviatyrannis era más bien un pequeño depredador bípedo.

facts.statement: The time range for Aviatyrannis is the Kimmeridgian stage, from 154.8 to 149.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Kimmeridgian (154.8 to 149.2 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The authors argue that, though more detailed study is needed, Aviatyrannis could be the earliest known ornithomimosaur and possibly the earliest known deinocheirid.
